findings.reason: the plan should promote `_path_coverage` to a shared reader that roadmap, flight and the dispatch summary all consume, instead of leaving flight to derive locally and roadmap to derive again.
findings.text: §3/§7 make the roadmap emit `coverage` (plans, live runs, head dispatchability) while `_path_coverage` already computes coverage over a critical path from live-pointer rows in `flight.py`, and `mcp_views.py:3506` already reads `row["coverage"]`; the roadmap would be a second implementation of one figure

findings.reason: naming `_path_coverage` (and its live-pointer input `_portfolio_live_rows`) turns the node into a promotion of existing owner code, which is the lower-risk change.
findings.text: the section names its three surfaces (roadmap, `crew(view="flight")`, dispatch summary) but not the mechanism that already produces coverage, `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage)`, so a node can rebuild the figure rather than move it

findings.reason: scoping the node to removing that audit comparison and adding the agreement assertion would stop it re-deriving a mechanism that is already shared.
findings.text: §10's measure, "one derivation answers `active_sprint_id` for every reader", already exists: `focus_sprint_id` at `reckon/project_state.py:1277` is the shared derivation and `reckon/roadmap.py:1988` (`_sprint_status_buckets`) already consumes it, so the only surviving duplicate is the audit's `active-sprint-mismatch` finding at `reckon/mcp.py:2321`

findings.reason: readers would conflate the routing-capability contract with the new followup classification, so the plan should rename the kind value or state why the existing field cannot carry it.
findings.text: §8 adds a `kind` field in {capability, measurement, record, repair} to `Followup`, whose model already carries `capability: CapabilityRequest` (line 1000) and a deprecated `tier`, and a kind value ("capability") collides by name with that existing attribute

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; §7, §8 and §10 extend existing readers (`roadmap.py`, `_schema.py`, `_plan_html.py`) and add a field, so there is no spread of shallow wrappers to weigh.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the roadmap `coverage` value duplicates `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage`, the existing owner of the coverage derivation, which portfolio flight already consumes.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §7/§3 add a `coverage` derivation to the roadmap without citing `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage`, which already computes exactly this from live pointers, and §10 proposes a "shared derivation" for `active_sprint_id` that already exists at `reckon/project_state.py:1277 focus_sprint_id`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §8 adds a followup `kind` field beside the existing `capability: CapabilityRequest` and deprecated `tier` fields on the same `Followup` model without saying why that vocabulary cannot be extended, and one kind value is itself named `capability`, colliding with that attribute.
